item.description: Fragment-based molecular design offers a chemically grounded strategy for exploring drug-like chemical space, yet identifying fragments that are both chemically feasible and relevant to a target property remains challenging. Fragment-level attribution is inherently ambiguous because each molecule contains multiple fragments and the same fragment can occur in molecular contexts with different property values. item.title: Manganese-Catalyzed Electrochemical Nitrogenative-Oxygenative Cleavage of Alkenes
item.description: Herein, we report a manganese-catalyzed electrochemical nitrogenative-oxygenative scission of olefins to nitriles and carbonyls. Mechanistic and kinetic studies reveal distinct precatalyst-activation and productive-turnover regimes, and support conversion of the manganese precursor into a mixed-valent oxo-bridged dimanganese(III/IV) species, followed by azide-dependent formation of a product-forming manganese species. Notably, polyunsaturated substrates can undergo alkene-chemoselective cleavage...

item.title: Liver Organoids as Human-Relevant Platforms for Hepatotoxicity Assessment
item.description: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) remains a major challenge in drug development because clinically relevant hepatotoxicity arises from integrated and context-dependent biological processes involving metabolic activation, transporter dysfunction, mitochondrial stress, immune signaling, and systemic regulation. Conventional preclinical models have provided important mechanistic insights but frequently fail to predict human outcomes, particularly in metabolism-dependent and idiosyncratic DILI, owing...

item.description: Copper phosphide (Cu(x)P), composed of earth-abundant elements, has been explored for advanced oxidation processes but suffers from ion leaching in acidic media and negligible activity under neutral and alkaline conditions, limiting its practical applicability. Here, we present a surface-state engineering strategy that systematically tunes the overlayer thickness and oxygen vacancy (OV) density of Cu(x)P through controlled Ar pretreatment. Here, redox-engineered polysaccharide nanoconjugates derived from low-molecular-weight heparin-doxorubicin conjugates coordinated with Fe³ ^(+) ions (LHDF NPs) are reported. item.title: Bioinspired Membrane Fusion-Gated Hydrogel Biosensor for Extraction-Free Viral RNA Detection of Infectious Influenza Virus
item.description: Emerging infectious diseases driven by zoonotic spillover demand rapid and reliable molecular diagnostics for pathogen identification and surveillance. However, conventional nucleic acid diagnostics cannot distinguish infectious virions from nonviable RNA fragments, limiting infectivity-resolved virus identification. Here, we report a bioinspired membrane-coated hydrogel (Memgel) sensor that enables extraction-free molecular detection of influenza virus while distinguishing fusion-competent...

item.title: Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided or Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided PCI for In-Stent Restenosis Lesions: Insights From the OCTIVUS Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: For the treatment of ISR lesions, OCT-guided PCI was associated with a lower risk of target-vessel failure than IVUS-guided PCI. However, given the exploratory nature of this analysis, these findings should not be considered clinically directive and warrant further investigation.

item.title: Left Atrial Stiffness Index and Prognosis Across Heart Failure Phenotypes in Acute Heart Failure: Insights from the STRATS-AHF Registry
item.description: CONCLUSION: In patients hospitalized for AHF, a higher LASI independently predicted all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization across HF phenotypes. Obtained from the admission echocardiogram, LASI captures an atrial component of risk that LVEF does not reflect, although part of this information overlaps with that of NT-proBNP; whether it can guide management remains to be tested.

item.title: Life Course Differences in Oral Health among Adults with Asthma: Analysis of the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
item.description: CONCLUSION: Adults with asthma, particularly middle-age and older adults, showed poorer oral health and functional characteristics than adults without asthma, supporting life-stage-specific oral care and targeted preventive dental hygiene strategies for adults with asthma.

item.title: FoRist: Three-DoF Soft Wearable Robot for Forearm and Wrist Assistance
item.description: The growing population of elderly individuals affected by musculoskeletal and neurological diseases experiences multijoint functional impairment, and individuals with compromised forearm and wrist function can lose independence and quality of life. However, most wearable robotic devices provide assistance for a single degree of freedom (DoF) and restrict other joint movements because decoupling multijoint kinematics remains challenging. This article introduces FoRist, a lightweight three-DoF...

item.title: One or 2 Veins in Head and Neck Free Flaps: A First-Principles Model
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The benefit of a second vein depends mainly on whether it can fail independently of the first. In the neck, a second vein from a separate venous system, drained into a separate recipient such as the external jugular system, should protect more than a second vena comitans joined to the same internal jugular trunk.

item.title: Asymmetric SWCNT/PFSA Bilayer Membranes Enhancing Performance and Mechanical Durability in PEM Fuel Cells
item.description: Thin perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) membranes are attractive for high-power polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells, but reduced thickness can aggravate dimensional instability and hydrogen crossover during hydration cycling. Here, an asymmetric bilayer membrane is designed by confining a functionalized single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT)/PFSA composite layer to one side of a continuous PFSA layer. item.title: Self-Resetting Liquid Metal Interfaces for Integrated DNA Capture, Release, and Recovery
item.description: Molecular separation is often limited not by binding efficiency alone, but by the need to independently manage capture, release, and recovery of the separation material. Conventional adsorbents typically retain a fixed material state, leaving molecular release and material recovery dependent on separate processing steps. Here, gallium-based liquid metal serves as a reconfigurable platform that couples these operations through pH-responsive changes in interfacial chemistry and physical state....

item.title: High Thermal Conductivity in Ultrathin Single-Crystalline BeO Films
item.description: Insulating materials featuring high thermal conductivity can enhance heat removal near the electron channel in modern transistors. Ultrawide bandgap beryllium oxide (BeO) is promising owing to its high bulk thermal conductivity, but its thermal transport in ultrathin films remains largely unexplored. This study investigates phonon thermal transport in ultrathin (<30 nm) single-crystalline (sc-) and nanocrystalline (nc-) BeO films grown by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) at 150°C...

item.title: Environmental burden of endoscopy-based gastric cancer screening in a national population-based program
item.description: CONCLUSION: Nationwide endoscopic screening for gastric cancer is associated with an increasing carbon footprint, particularly among younger populations. Integrating environmental considerations into future screening strategies may be necessary to balance clinical benefits with long-term healthcare sustainability.

item.title: Genetic Diagnoses in an Adult Cohort of Predominantly Antibody Deficiency in Australia
item.description: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Predominantly antibody deficiencies (PAD) are the most common IEI. Despite advances in genomics, the diagnostic yield in adults remains below 40%, leaving most patients without a molecular diagnosis to guide clinical management. We aimed to define the spectrum of causative genetic variants in adult PAD patients.

item.description: Red blood cell transfusion is life-saving but is constrained by immune incompatibility and limited availability, as red blood cells are derived primarily from donor blood. In vitro production of red blood cells from human stem cells provides a promising solution, though an optimized differentiation protocol has yet to be established. The protocols for erythroid differentiation included treatment of CD34+ cells with mTOR modulators, specifically MHY-1485 as an activator and rapamycin as an...

item.description: Study DesignSystematic Review.ObjectivesTo characterize assessment methods for psoas-based or skeletal muscle mass measures and spine-specific paraspinal muscle measures, and to synthesize their associations with postoperative outcomes after adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery.MethodsPubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched for studies published from January 1, 1980, to March 1, 2026. item.title: Rethinking chronic wound healing biomaterials toward integrated therapeutic platforms
item.description: Chronic wounds such as diabetic ulcers and pressure sores are governed by a self-perpetuating pathological cycle of persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, bacterial infection and biofilm formation, and impaired angiogenesis. Conventional dressings, designed mainly for physical protection and exudate management, cannot sense or respond to this evolving microenvironment, and single-function biomaterials address only isolated aspects of the problem. Wound care is now moving toward platforms...

item.title: Mechanistic design principles for homogeneous methane-to-methanol oxidation
item.description: Selective oxidation of methane to methanol represents one of the most important and challenging transformations in sustainable chemistry, as it offers a direct route for converting abundant methane resources into value-added liquid fuels. However, the high C-H bond dissociation energy of methane, which is approximately 105 kcal mol^(-1) and the greater susceptibility of methanol and other partially oxidised products toward further oxidation make high activity and selectivity difficult to achieve...

item.title: BFVD v3-the atlas of predicted viral protein structures
item.description: The Big Fantastic Virus Database (BFVD) v3 is the most comprehensive resource for ColabFold-AlphaFold2-predicted viral protein structures. It holds 5 776 417 structures of nearly all viral sequences in UniProt 2025_03, a 16.4-fold increase compared to the representative-only catalogs of BFVD v1 and v2. Structure prediction quality has also improved, with high-confidence predictions accounting for 75.3% of BFVD v3 entries. item.title: Developmental processes linking depressive symptoms, positive parenting, and parent-adolescent shared time across the pre- to post-COVID-19 pandemic periods among Korean adolescents
item.description: Previous research links adolescent depressive symptoms to positive parenting and parent-adolescent shared time. However, their longitudinal associations across the pandemic era remain less understood, particularly among Korean adolescents. This study examined longitudinal changes and prospective associations among these constructs across the pre-, during-, and post-pandemic periods. item.title: Dismissive attitudes and perceived peer and staff accountability in cyber and physical sexual violence perpetration among high school students
item.description: Adolescent sexual violence (SV) perpetration occurs across physical and digital contexts, yet less is known about when dismissive attitudes are more strongly associated with perpetration in each setting. Guided by a reasoned-action framework, this nonpreregistered secondary analysis examined perceived peer and staff accountability as correlates of perpetration and moderators of the attitude-perpetration association. item.description: CONCLUSION: Vickers hardness of TC85 resin under the studied conditions was not significantly affected by the post-curing duration under a nitrogen environment. TC20 showed the greatest overall recovery response.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Japanese real-world evidence describes generally favorable long-term outcomes following intravesical BCG therapy for HR-NMIBC but also reveals substantial heterogeneity in implementation, treatment exposure, and completion. item.title: Changes in combustible cigarette, heated tobacco product and electronic cigarette use and cardiovascular risk among adults with type 2 diabetes: A Korean national retrospective cohort study
item.description: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Heated tobacco products (HTPs) and electronic cigarettes (ECs) are increasingly used as alternatives to combustible cigarettes (CCs), but their cardiovascular implications in type 2 diabetes remain unclear. We examined the associations between changes in smoking patterns, including self-reported changes from CCs to HTPs and/or ECs between two health screenings, and subsequent cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk among smokers with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes.

item.title: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw after denosumab following prior osteoporosis therapy in rheumatic diseases
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Prior IV BP exposure and clinical or dental comorbidities were associated with a higher frequency of MRONJ after transition to denosumab in patients with rheumatic diseases. Given the retrospective design and small number of events, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Careful dental evaluation and multidisciplinary management are warranted when planning sequential osteoporosis therapies.

item.title: Clinical features of moderate-to-severe antibiotic allergy in Korea: analysis from the drug allergy safety information sharing system database
item.description: CONCLUSION: Immediate antibiotic allergy in Korea was mainly caused by β-lactams, with cefaclor identified as the leading culprit for severe reactions. Delayed reactions were characterized by a relatively greater contribution of non-β-lactam antibiotics than immediate reactions.

item.title: Aspergillus positivity in lower respiratory specimens as a predictor of poor prognosis in invasive pulmonary aspergillosis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Aspergillus species isolation from LRT specimens was associated with greater microbiologic burden, more severe radiologic features, and higher mortality. Culture positivity may serve as a readily available prognostic marker in IPA.

item.title: Syncope as a predictor of sudden cardiac arrest: a nationwide population-based study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Syncope may be a surrogate marker of future SCA. The association was attenuated after adjusting for various confounders. The risk increased by 91% and 29% before and after adjustment, respectively. Individuals with prior syncope, older age, male sex, and cardiometabolic disorders had a higher risk of future SCA.

item.title: The efficacy and safety of on-label reduced-dose apixaban in patients with atrial fibrillation in real-world practice
item.description: CONCLUSION: The INSPIRE study provides real-world evidence supporting guideline-directed reduced-dose apixaban in Asian populations, while identifying high-risk subgroups requiring careful patient selection and individualized management strategies.

item.description: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is an important opportunistic fungal infection in immunocompromised hosts. Although its incidence has declined markedly in people with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) following the widespread use of antiretroviral therapy and prophylaxis, PJP is increasingly encountered in HIV-negative patients receiving immunosuppressive or targeted immunomodulatory therapies. item.title: Gastroesophageal reflux disease as a comorbidity in chronic lung diseases: mechanism, clinical impacts and therapeutic uncertainty
item.description: Chronic lung diseases, particularly chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and interstitial lung disease, are major contributors to global morbidity and mortality. Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is highly prevalent in these populations and has been implicated in exacerbations and disease progression. item.description: Progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) represents a progressive phenotype across various fibrosing interstitial lung diseases (ILDs). The epidemiology of PPF is confounded by differences in the defining criteria for PPF, data capture sources, as well as the heterogeneity of ILD subtype diagnoses. In Asian PPF cohorts, although some heterogeneity exists across countries, connective tissue disease (CTD)-associated ILD is the most frequently identified underlying cause of PPF. item.title: Epidemiology of interstitial lung diseases in Asia
item.description: The epidemiology of interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) in Asia has gained increasing attention with the emergence of new population- based datasets and national registries. Current evidence demonstrates that the burden and subtype distribution of ILDs vary considerably across regions, reflecting differences in genetic susceptibility, environmental or occupational exposure, and healthcare infrastructure. item.title: 2026 Consensus on the Management of Cushing's Disease: A Collaborative Statement from the Korean Endocrine Society and Japan Endocrine Society
item.description: The primary treatment goal of Cushing's disease (CD) is sustained normalization of hypercortisolism as well as relief of tumor mass effects, to reduce morbidity and mortality and improve long-term quality of life. Korea and Japan share broadly similar therapeutic principles for CD; however, real-world management differs because of country-specific healthcare systems, regulatory environments, and medication availability. item.description: Suboptimal diet is a major modifiable risk factor for non-communicable diseases (NCDs), but its burden in Spain has not been quantified with Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates. We extracted GBD 2023 estimates of diet-attributable deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for 15 dietary risks among adults aged ≥25 years in Spain (1990-2023) and applied joinpoint regression and Das Gupta decomposition. item.description: Opioids have been widely used as potent pain relievers however, repeated use can cause side effects. Above all, tolerance and dependence are perhaps the most prominent problems. Tolerance leads to a decrease in the analgesic effects and an increase in the patient's demand for drugs. This study investigated if acupuncture could inhibit the development of tolerance of opioid analgesic. item.description: Operator competence is central to the safety of ultrasound-guided procedures in pain management. In Korean medicine, ultrasound-guided pharmacopuncture is increasingly used as an interventional pain procedure; however, to our knowledge, no procedure-specific competency assessment tool has been developed for this intervention. item.description: CONCLUSION: This QI initiative improved early colostrum administration and was associated with improvements in clinical outcomes, including NEC, despite no significant increase in overall MoM use.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Multiparametric MRI-based voxel-wise habitat analysis enables accurate, noninvasive differentiation of non-enhancing glioblastoma from low-grade glioma while demonstrating potential prognostic relevance based on intratumoral physiologic heterogeneity.

item.description: In recent years, the use of document information to predict compound activity has gained attention. However, existing methods face challenges in applying these predictions to compounds not included in the training data because of the shortage and insufficient applicability of chemical knowledge as well as in interpreting the basis for predictions. item.title: Efficacy and Safety of Mirikizumab After Switching From Ustekinumab in Crohn's Disease: Results From the VIVID-2 Extension Study
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Mirikizumab, an anti-interleukin-23p19 monoclonal antibody, was safe and efficacious in patients with moderately-to-severely active Crohn's disease (CD) in the placebo- and active-controlled (ustekinumab) phase 3 VIVID-1 study. Here we report efficacy and safety for ustekinumab endoscopic non-responders from VIVID-1 who switched to open-label mirikizumab in VIVID-2.

item.title: Proton-conducting ionic crystal composed of a hydrogen-bonded cobalt(III) biimidazole complex and Keggin-type polyoxometalate
item.description: An ionic crystal, [Co^(III)(H(2)bim)(3)][PMo(12)O(40)] (1), composed of a hydrogen-bonded cobalt(iii) biimidazole complex and a Keggin-type polyoxometalate, was synthesised. The ionic crystal retained its crystalline framework upon solvent removal and exhibited reversible water adsorption/desorption. Under humid conditions, water uptake generated a hydrated state that exhibited a high proton conductivity of 8.85 × 10^(-3) S cm^(-1) at 75 °C and 100% RH.

item.title: Transposon insertion sequencing identifies genetic determinants of intrinsic rifamycin resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus
item.description: Mycobacterium abscessus exhibits intrinsic resistance to many antimicrobial agents, including rifampicin, a frontline anti-tuberculosis drug, severely limiting treatment options. Here, we used transposon insertion sequencing (Tn-Seq) to perform a genome-wide screen to identify genes required for intrinsic rifampicin resistance in M. abscessus. item.description: NAD^(+) is a central metabolic cofactor and substrate for NAD^(+)-dependent enzymes that regulate cellular stress responses, DNA repair, and senescence. item.title: Gastric juice, but not fecal microbiota, reflects gastric mucosal microbial profiles in patients with early gastric neoplasia: implications for minimally invasive sampling
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Gastric juice closely reflects gastric mucosal microbial profiles and may represent a feasible biopsy-sparing surrogate for gastric sampling. These findings support the further evaluation of gastric juice-based microbiota profiling as a minimally invasive approach for biomarker development and risk stratification in gastric neoplasia.

item.title: Design and synthesis of maresin 1 analogues using the conformational properties of biaryl scaffolds
item.description: To improve the chemical stability of maresin 1, analogues with biaryl scaffolds replacing the unstable triene moiety were designed based on conformational analysis. One analogue showed potent anti-inflammatory activity and improved metabolic stability.

item.description: Although heavy-ion beam irradiation has been applied to microalgae to develop strains for industrial applications, the effects of irradiation, including comprehensive mutation profiling, remain poorly characterized at the genome-wide level. In this study, we analyzed mutations using sequencing data from 12 strains of the haptophyte Tisochrysis lutea, isolated after carbon-ion beam irradiation. item.description: Gastrointestinal transit time is a major ecological determinant of the human gut microbiome, yet causal evidence that disentangles the effects of diet from those of the gut environment remains limited. item.description: Most CRISPR-Cas9 design tools select guide RNAs (gRNAs) by ranking predefined candidates rather than actively optimizing them. Here we instead formulate SpCas9 spacer refinement as a constrained search problem, in which a limited number of nucleotide substitutions may be introduced outside the PAM-proximal seed region. item.description: Proteins are highly diverse functional polymers where the specific sequence of amino acids, selected from a standard genetically encoded alphabet of 20 (C20), determines the structure and ultimately the function of the resulting folded protein. item.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Viral Nanobody Epitope Prediction
item.description: Rapid development of therapeutics against emerging viral pathogens increasingly depends on machine learning (ML), both to generate candidate binders and for structural validation. Nanobodies (Nbs), or single-domain antibodies, are promising antiviral therapeutics, but accurate in silico prediction of viral epitopes remains challenging. item.description: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) plays a central role in metabolic regulation and is a major therapeutic target for obesity and diabetes. item.title: Instance-Wise Contrastive Graph Neural Network Enables the Discovery of Novel Aedes aegypti Larvicidal Compounds
item.description: Aedes aegypti remains a major arboviral vector, making larval control a critical strategy to reduce mosquito populations. item.title: Implementation of a trauma-informed, social-ecological approach to student suicide prevention: a case study and future recommendations
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Addressing suicide on college campuses will require intervention at multiple levels. The implementation of trauma-informed and SESPM-guided programming can inform future efforts on other campuses.

item.title: Longitudinal Changes in Thyroid Hormone Levels in Psychiatric Patients After Risperidone or Olanzapine Monotherapy: A One-Year Follow-Up Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: After risperidone or olanzapine monotherapy, patients showed significant alterations in thyroid hormone levels (decreased free thyroxine, early decreased total thyroxine, and progressively increased TSH), with 3.48% developing overt thyroid dysfunction. These preliminary results suggest that vigilance regarding thyroid function should be maintained.

item.title: Outcomes in a Cohort of Preterm Infants Born at 22-23 Weeks From a Proactive Center in Germany
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this experienced center with an intensive care treatment approach, survival of infants born at 22 + 0 to 23 + 6 weeks GA was high. However, neonatal morbidity and neurodevelopmental impairment remained substantial, particularly among 22-week infants. Future efforts should focus on improving long-term outcomes in addition to survival.

item.title: Temporal Heterogeneity and Driving Factors of Idiopathic Epilepsy Incidence in BRICS Countries: A Population-Based Age-Period-Cohort Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Idiopathic epilepsy incidence in BRICS countries demonstrates significant heterogeneity. Temporal trends are shaped by perinatal health, demographic changes, healthcare improvements, and sociocultural factors. Targeted interventions for high-risk populations are critical to reduce disease burden and optimize resource allocation.

item.title: Predictors of outcomes of endoscopic sinus surgery for CRSwNP: a systematic review of the literature
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This review may assist clinicians in identifying patients at higher risk of poor outcomes after ESS, contributing to more precise and personalised medical care.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Patients with PSA are at increased risk of epilepsy, regardless of age, sex, and stroke type.

The fusion retained the KMT2A (alias: mixed-lineage leukemia [MLL]) CxxC domain and ETS proto-oncogene1 (ETS1) DNA-binding domain (ED), indicating potential aberrant transcriptional regulation. item.title: The long non-coding RNA lncWOX5 modulates auxin-responsive adventitious root formation in poplar
item.description: Adventitious root (AR) formation requires coordinated auxin signaling and developmental reprogramming, yet how the magnitude and timing of this response are modulated remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the function of the poplar (Populus deltoides × P. euramericana, clone 'Nanlin 895') long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) lncWOX5 using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated loss-of-function analyses together with previously reported gain-of-function evidence. Independent lncWOX5 knockout lines showed...

item.title: Efficiency, Efficacy, and Energy-Specific Safety of Pulsed Field Versus Thermal Ablation in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Insights From Contemporary Randomized Data (the E<sup>3</sup>-PFA Collaboration)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PFA provides greater procedural efficiency, improved peri-procedural safety, and a lower risk of atrial arrhythmia recurrence than pooled thermal ablation in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The efficacy advantage was primarily driven by comparisons with cryoballoon ablation, whereas outcomes were comparable between PFA and contemporary RFA.

item.title: Treadmill Walking Differentially Modulates Early Auditory Responses to Standard and Deviant Sounds
item.description: People often encounter environmental sounds while walking without attending to them, but it is unclear whether walking alters early cortical responses to these sounds. We recorded 32-channel electroencephalography from 22 healthy young adults during a passive auditory frequency-oddball paradigm. Conditions were sitting and treadmill walking without an object, with a water-filled cup or with a clay-filled cup matched for mass and apparent fill height. item.title: Machine learning-assisted single-system multichannel sensor for the recognition of ochratoxins
item.description: An albumin-based single-system multichannel sensor was developed for the discrimination of ochratoxins with the aid of machine learning.

item.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes Following Smartwatch Irregular Rhythm Notification: Findings From the Apple Heart Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Receipt of a smartwatch IRN was associated with higher odds of subsequent self-reported cardiovascular events beyond atrial fibrillation. These findings suggest that IRNs may identify individuals at elevated short-term cardiovascular risk.

item.title: Clinical translation of viral targeting of the endothelium in pulmonary vascular diseases
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary vascular diseases are characterized by endothelial dysfunction and progressive vascular remodeling. Most pulmonary vascular diseases, such as pulmonary hypertension, are rare but fatal. Although current therapies improve hemodynamics and clinical outcomes, they do not consistently restore endothelial homeostasis or reverse vascular remodeling, highlighting the potential of gene therapy as a disease-modifying strategy.

item.title: Translons upstream of protein-coding regions rather than their products are crucial for proliferation of human cells of distinct origin
item.description: Upstream open reading frames (uORFs) are a widespread class of translated regions (translons) occurring in 5' leaders of messenger RNAs. They serve critical roles in post-transcriptional regulation and some are known to encode small proteins and peptideins. Yet it is not known which of these modes of function is more critical for human cells. item.title: Reprogramming mRNA localization by targeted RNA-protein interference reveals roles in oncogenesis
item.description: RNA binding proteins (RBPs) associate with RNAs in intricate ribonucleoprotein complexes and regulate various aspects of RNA life cycle and, by extension, cell functions. Despite their significance, elucidating the functional contributions of specific RNA-RBP binding events, particularly in long-term phenotypic assays, remains challenging. item.title: Genomic Diversity, Autozygosity and Candidate Selection Regions in the Indigenous Kyrgyz Taigan Sighthound Revealed by Whole-Genome Sequencing
item.description: The Kyrgyz Taigan is an indigenous Central Asian sighthound whose genomic diversity remains largely uncharacterised. We sequenced the whole genomes of 20 Taigan dogs from five localities across Kyrgyzstan and, after removal of two duplicate-level samples, analysed 18 of them together with 12 publicly available genomes from other breeds, using 12.48 million autosomal SNPs. item.title: Interosseous membrane stimulation for neuropathic and musculoskeletal pain in Veterans: real-world clinical outcomes from a retrospective case review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Substantial immediate pain reduction with IMS was observed and may offer an accessible nonpharmacologic intervention for neuropathic and musculoskeletal pain.
